column1: # version<TAB>ProductCode<TAB>UpgradeCode  -- the IDENTITY of each PUBLISHED .msi.
# WHY THIS LEDGER EXISTS. The .wxs uses <Product Id="*">, so wixl mints a BRAND NEW ProductCode
# on every single build. Two .msi files with the same ProductVersion are therefore DIFFERENT
# products to Windows, and the same-version row in the Upgrade table refuses to install one over
# the other ("... is already installed. There is nothing to do.").
# That means: build the .msi ONCE per version and publish THAT FILE. Rebuilding and re-uploading
# under the same version strands anyone who downloaded the first one -- they cannot upgrade and
# cannot cleanly reinstall. It happened on 2026-10-17: the 2.0.15 msi was built at 01:24, attached
# to the release, then rebuilt at 04:40 and clobbered the asset.
# verify_msi_upgrade.ps1 checks the published asset against this file, so a silent re-upload
# fails CI instead of reaching a player.
# UpgradeCode must be IDENTICAL on every row. It is the only thing tying an old install to the
# new one; a change there leaves every existing install on disk as a second, parallel product.
# 2.0.17 reserved from the uploaded draft prerelease asset (2026-10-27), already shared
# with testers. Keep this identity even before publication; do not rebuild this version.
